arcFigures.details: Duke-level former battlefield commander. Studies current Marquises through engineered battlefields rather than relying on simple overpowering.
skills: Turns terrain, civilians, supplies and timing into constraints tailored to a target's martial strengths.
Creates multiple plausible battle routes so an opponent reveals decision habits.
Coordinates distributed fighters through subtle qi pulses rather than visible signals.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc IV — Moonless City & Marquis War

arcFigures.name: Qiao Ren
arcFigures.subtitle: The Golden Fox · Season 16
arcFigures.details: High-Marquis information broker whose greatest weapon is rumor architecture and political leverage.
skills: Maps favors, rumors and political incentives into exploitable networks.
Builds lies almost entirely from individually true statements.
Uses crowds and prepared social confusion to disappear without direct confrontation.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc IV — Moonless City & Marquis War

arcFigures.name: Jiang Taixuan
arcFigures.subtitle: The Uncrowned Emperor · Unranked sovereign · Seasons 18–22
arcFigures.details: A far-northern sovereign who rejected the public ranking system. Strong enough to gravely injure #2 Liang Yue and force #1 Kael into a serious clean fight, but still separated from Rhen by an absurd, effectively immeasurable gulf.
skills: Nine adaptive circulation layers distribute and reroute incoming force, allowing Jiang to remain functional under Duke-level punishment.
Compresses force into a small contact point and disrupts the meridian route beneath impact.
Uses elite formations and simultaneous crises to force stronger opponents into costly moral choices.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc V — The Black Sun Saga

arcFigures.name: Duan He
arcFigures.subtitle: The Iron Rain General · Black Sun commander
arcFigures.details: Upper-Marquis battlefield specialist whose throwing-spears use silk-steel lines, recoil and moving anchors to create changing attack geometry.
skills: Twelve short spears attack through controlled lines and prepared recoil angles.
Coordinates multiple spear teams through moving anchor riders.
Sacrifices the spear harness to break contact when a stronger fighter closes distance.
arcFigures.firstEpisodeTitle: The Duke of the Black Storm
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc V — The Black Sun Saga

arcFigures.name: Mi Suyun
arcFigures.subtitle: The Red Loom Strategist · Black Sun commander
arcFigures.details: Formation strategist whose network shares timing information across units. A natural tactical rival for Sera rather than a raw-power peer.
skills: Qi filaments distribute timing and response information across prepared soldiers.
Changes an entire formation's response through a single command knot.
Severs her own network instantly to prevent an opponent from tracing it back to her.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc V — The Black Sun Saga
arcFigures.strength: Strategist — exact cultivation not formally rated

arcFigures.name: Qiu Shen
arcFigures.subtitle: The Hollow Ox · Black Sun bridge-holder
arcFigures.details: Lower-Marquis body cultivator built to hold terrain and delay stronger opponents long enough for armies to move.
skills: Four rotating internal chains lock stance and distribute impact into the ground.
A short-range shoulder impact using all four internal pillars at once.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc V — The Black Sun Saga

arcFigures.name: Zhao Renkai
arcFigures.subtitle: The Ash-Marked General · Black Sun field commander
arcFigures.details: A near-#6 field commander whose strength is endurance logistics rather than explosive dueling.
skills: Rotates fatigue and qi burden across units so an army can march far beyond normal endurance.
Transfers route and rest changes through prepared standards without courier delay.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc V — The Black Sun Saga
arcFigures.strength: Field commander — exact cultivation not formally rated

arcFigures.name: Mo Qingzhao
arcFigures.subtitle: The Paper Emperor · World Rank #7
arcFigures.details: Male independent martial scholar using reinforced paper and qi-thread formations.
skills: Reinforces prepared paper for cutting, shielding, restraint and formation control.
Scattered pages unfold into intersecting cutting planes and containment geometry.
Hair-thin qi threads reposition prepared paper pieces.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc VI — The Ranking Succession

arcFigures.name: Yun Shizhen
arcFigures.subtitle: The Pale Venom · World Rank #10
arcFigures.details: Frail-looking poison sovereign with extraordinary toxin immunity and battlefield contamination control.
skills: Conditions body and meridians against progressively stronger toxins.
Different toxin families attack muscle, perception, blood, fatigue, pain and qi circulation.
Refines a foreign poison and returns a modified version through contact.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc VI — The Ranking Succession

arcFigures.name: Mu Gyeong
arcFigures.subtitle: The Heaven-Eater · Nine Graves enforcer
arcFigures.details: High-Marquis anti-qi specialist.
skills: Consumes ambient qi, making conventional techniques harder to sustain.
Expands the furnace radius at severe internal cost.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc VI — The Ranking Succession

arcFigures.name: Seo Mujin
arcFigures.subtitle: The Grave Sovereign · Nine Graves leader
arcFigures.details: Institutional saboteur relying on archived counters and succession intelligence rather than Duke-level force.
skills: Historical responses to known martial systems.
Pulls circulation toward recorded historical patterns.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc VI — The Ranking Succession

arcFigures.name: Gu Xian
arcFigures.subtitle: The Scripture Thief · Seasons 28–32
arcFigures.details: Upper-Marquis forbidden cultivator who transplants fragments of cultivation architecture from dying martial artists into compatible recipients. His forbidden method enables Huo Wujin to assimilate Jiang Taixuan's circulation principles.
skills: Extracts and transplants fragments of cultivation architecture from a dying martial artist's meridian network.
Attempts to force a foreign circulation route into an opponent through touch, disrupting established flow.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc VII — The Empty Throne

arcFigures.name: Tae Muyeon
arcFigures.subtitle: The Horizon King · Unranked co-#1
arcFigures.details: Unranked sovereign considered roughly comparable to Kael on the right battlefield. Boundless Horizon manipulates engagement distance through movement geometry rather than teleportation.
skills: Controls engagement range by altering approach rhythm and movement geometry.
Heaven Is Always One Step Away
Maintains ideal striking distance while denying the opponent clean completion of their final measure.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc VII — The Empty Throne

arcFigures.name: Sorin Vael
arcFigures.subtitle: Crown V · The Weightless Tyrant · Deceased · assassinated by Ancient King VII Orun Vhal
arcFigures.details: Lowest-ranked elite Crown, yet above any single Duke in raw threat. Leaves #7–#10 critical; Sera cannot defeat him but successfully redirects the battle long enough to evacuate the wounded.
skills: Redirects contact force into unexpected directions.
Forces committed force in his combat field to resolve along a chosen direction.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc VIII Part I — The Six Crowns: Western Dark
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Crown V — The Weightless Tyrant (lowest Crown)

arcFigures.name: Valeria Nox
arcFigures.subtitle: Crown IV · Saint of the Last Step · Deceased · assassinated by Ancient King VII Orun Vhal
arcFigures.details: Crown IV, decisively above a single Duke. There Is No Final Step learns deliberate endings and denies them; she also uses calculated cruelty against bystanders and wounded opponents to force predictable emotional responses. Lei survives her repeatedly through adaptation but never defeats her.
skills: Learns committed martial sequences and denies their final step.
For a short span, deliberate martial actions fail immediately before their intended completion.
arcFigures.firstEpisodeTitle: The Saint of the Last Step
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc VIII Part I — The Six Crowns: Western Dark
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Crown IV — Saint of the Last Step

arcFigures.name: Draven Sol
arcFigures.subtitle: Crown III · The Red God · Deceased
arcFigures.details: Uses Crimson Dominion Body to convert active trauma into short-term reinforcement. Gravely injures Sera before Rhen returns. Killed by Rhen after One Petal Before Dawn disables the trauma-power dependency.
skills: Active injury temporarily increases reinforcement and output.
God Born From His Own Corpse
Treats multiple active injuries as simultaneous power sources.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc VIII Part I — The Six Crowns: Western Dark
arcFigures.strength: Crown III combatant — exact cultivation not formally rated

arcFigures.name: Ilyra Serath
arcFigures.subtitle: The Mirror Queen · Former Crown II · Current World #6
arcFigures.details: Former Crown II who abandons her western identity before the Ancient Kings awaken, surviving Orun's purge because she is no longer part of the Crown system. She accepts Sera's vacant #6 seat, is stronger than several Dukes in direct combat during the invasion, and becomes the coalition's central protector.
skills: Left and right meridian systems learn complementary responses.
Both halves operate almost like two martial artists sharing one consciousness.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc VIII Part I — The Six Crowns: Western Dark
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Former Crown II — now World #6, The Mirror Queen

arcFigures.name: Aurel Veyr
arcFigures.subtitle: Crown I · The First Catastrophe · Deceased · assassinated by Ancient King VII Orun Vhal
arcFigures.details: Crown I and strongest subordinate. Decisively defeats Tae and later Kael, proving the upper Crowns individually outrank even the two Number Ones.
skills: Extreme refinement of martial fundamentals with almost no wasted action.
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc VIII Part I — The Six Crowns: Western Dark
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Crown I — The First Catastrophe (strongest subordinate)

arcFigures.name: Vaelor Veyr
arcFigures.subtitle: Leader · The Crown Beyond Crowns · Deceased · assassinated by Ancient King VII Orun Vhal
arcFigures.details: Leader of the Six Crowns. Cruelly crushes all Five Dukes together, tortures Lei close to death, then outmaneuvers Kael and Tae together and leaves both near death before Rhen arrives. In Season 43 he warns of much older western powers.
skills: Multiple body regions possess semi-independent circulation authority.
Six major circulation authorities operate simultaneously.
Seventh original circulation authority governing the outer six.
arcFigures.firstEpisodeTitle: The Crown Beyond Crowns Is Moving
arcFigures.firstArc: Arc VIII Part II — The Six Crowns: Crown Beyond Crowns

arcFigures.name: Orun Vhal
arcFigures.subtitle: Ancient King VII · The Buried Sovereign · Deceased · life force consumed by Aethon
arcFigures.details: Weakest of the Seven Ancient Kings, yet drastically above Vaelor. Orun's Earth Burial cultivation turns natural earth, stone, dust and sand into extensions of his martial body: force can be deposited into terrain, accumulated for centuries and released later. He became legendary after storing seven years of force throughout a capital, then returning it through the earth when twelve grandmasters invaded, erasing their army and reshaping the valley. Begins the invasion by assassinating Vaelor, Aurel, Valeria and Sorin alone.
skills: Natural earth, stone, dust and sand can carry fragments of Orun's internal strength and remember force deposited into them.
Stores martial force inside terrain, objects and carried stones, then releases accumulated impacts through the earth from multiple directions.
Pulverizes surrounding stone and soil into a qi-saturated sand sea; every grain carries a fragment of buried force, making movement itself trigger countless small impacts.
While connected to natural ground, Orun can divert part of incoming damage into the surrounding earth. Severing him from terrain sharply reduces this defense.
The World Beneath Your Feet Is Mine
Claims kilometres of natural terrain as one burial domain. Earth, stone, dust and sand collapse toward chosen targets while attempts to smash through the domain feed fresh impact into Buried Heaven.
arcFigures.firstArc: Final Major Arc Part I — The Seven Thrones
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Ancient King VII — The Buried Sovereign (weakest King)

arcFigures.name: Iscaryn Voss
arcFigures.subtitle: Ancient King VI · The Thousand-Road King · Deceased · life force consumed by Aethon
arcFigures.details: A nomadic challenger who walked the western world for nearly two centuries. Became King after striking seven distant capitals in one night through routes he had previously travelled. Every historical path he has personally crossed can become a future movement route.
skills: Any route Iscaryn has physically traversed becomes a reusable movement or attack path.
arcFigures.firstEpisodeTitle: King VI Walks an Old Road
arcFigures.firstArc: Final Major Arc Part I — The Seven Thrones
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Ancient King VI — The Thousand-Road King

arcFigures.name: Rhavenn Korr
arcFigures.subtitle: Ancient King V · The Nine-Lived King · Deceased · life force consumed by Aethon
arcFigures.details: Cultivation heretic who deliberately destroyed and rebuilt his own cultivation nine times using completely different foundations. Eight execution forces believed they killed him during the War of Nine Graves; each time another cultivated life took over. His ninth life synthesizes the lessons of the previous eight.
skills: Nine complete cultivation architectures coexist in one body; destroying one does not end the others.
arcFigures.firstArc: Final Major Arc Part I — The Seven Thrones
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Ancient King V — The Nine-Lived King

arcFigures.name: Tor Veydan
arcFigures.subtitle: Ancient King IV · The Last-Breath King · Deceased · life force consumed by Aethon
arcFigures.details: Born with a body whose natural output should have killed him young. He perfected the flaw instead. His coronation legend says he fought an army for three days after physicians gave him one hour to live; centuries later, he still has not spent his final breath.
skills: Compresses centuries of hypothetical future physical potential into present bursts, creating enormous deferred bodily debt.
arcFigures.firstArc: Final Major Arc Part I — The Seven Thrones
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Ancient King IV — The Last-Breath King

arcFigures.name: Caedros Marr
arcFigures.subtitle: Ancient King III · The Nameless King · Deceased · life force consumed by Aethon
arcFigures.details: Former archivist denied the legendary arts he recorded. He learned to sever the martial identity that lets a practitioner reproduce a named technique, then stripped the Twelve Sacred Masters of their signature arts and ended their monopoly.
skills: After comprehending a named art's defining identity, Caedros severs the practitioner's ability to reproduce that exact architecture.
arcFigures.firstArc: Final Major Arc Part I — The Seven Thrones
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Ancient King III — The Nameless King

arcFigures.name: Varesh Nhal
arcFigures.subtitle: Ancient King II · The Heaven-Crushing King · Deceased · life force consumed by Aethon
arcFigures.details: A physical monster even among Ancient Kings. Killed a city-destroying war beast barehanded and became King after five sovereign challengers left his coronation battlefield as a canyon. His raw strength drastically exceeds Vaelor before his signature escalation even begins.
skills: Every consecutive physical exchange increases the destructive force of Varesh's next impact until the chain is broken.
arcFigures.firstEpisodeTitle: King II Arrives Without an Art
arcFigures.firstArc: Final Major Arc Part I — The Seven Thrones
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Ancient King II — The Heaven-Crushing King

arcFigures.name: Amon Serath
arcFigures.subtitle: Ancient King I · The King of the Dying Sun · Deceased · life force consumed by Aethon
arcFigures.details: Strongest of the Seven Kings. His fire consumes life qi instead of ordinary matter. Three sovereigns attacked his coronation together and survived physically while their cultivation aged decades within minutes. Even the Rhen-trained eastern coalition loses catastrophically to him.
skills: Burns the life qi sustaining body and cultivation; stronger opponents provide more fuel.
Ignites life qi inside the meridians of everyone beneath Amon's dark-red martial sun.
arcFigures.firstArc: Final Major Arc Part I — The Seven Thrones
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Ancient King I — The King of the Dying Sun (strongest King)

arcFigures.name: Aethon Vael
arcFigures.subtitle: Ancient Overlord · The Sovereign Before Heaven · Appears 25 · Deceased · ended by Petals Beneath a Frozen Moon
arcFigures.details: Mythical young man with extremely long white hair who appears unchanged across records separated by centuries. Every Ancient King became legendary independently, then eventually challenged Aethon and lost. He sees roughly seven seconds into branching combat futures, permanently adapts to survived martial phenomena, and regenerates toward a remembered perfected body. Final enemy of the major saga.
skills: Continuously sees roughly seven seconds into branching probable futures.
Surviving a martial phenomenon causes permanent adaptation to its underlying principle.
Reconstructs his damaged body toward an internally remembered perfected state while central consciousness remains intact.
Drains the life force, cultivation and signature principles of all Seven Kings and incorporates them into himself.
arcFigures.firstArc: Final Major Arc Part II — The Sovereign Before Heaven
arcFigures.affiliationRole: The Sovereign Before Heaven — above the Seven Kings

arcFigures.name: Aldric Veyrhald
arcFigures.subtitle: The Unbroken Standard · Established Paragon · Leader of Veyrhald
arcFigures.details: The public leader of Veyrhald and the strongest revealed authority in Southern Isgard, holding the First Banner's legal authority through the Gate Seal. He is not eager for massacre; his danger comes from believing stable Ledger law requires Wuyue's submission after they destroyed a ranked Guild and left Isgard without answering for it. Final arc: survives the Shinsei invasion but is critically injured in early Phase II.
skills: Supreme Domain Skill · Domain / Sustained Offense
Once Aldric honestly commits an attack and achieves contact, its martial force continues until he ends it or an opposing Domain destroys its governing principle.
arcFigures.affiliationRole: First Banner leader — Southern Isgard’s strongest revealed authority

arcFigures.name: Sigrun Veyrhald
arcFigures.subtitle: The First Wall · Newly ascended Paragon · Veyrhald field commander
arcFigures.details: Veyrhald’s foremost battlefield defender. She turns a line’s history of surviving pressure into the foundation that lets it survive again, making every failed breakthrough strengthen the next defence. After the Wuyue war Sigrun ascends from Peak Sovereign to a newly ascended Paragon; her Domain remains pending and must be a named Dominion. Final arc: a newly ascended Paragon whose Graven Dominion and Last Body Standing hold an evacuation; she survives but is critically injured in the Shinsei opening invasion.
skills: The First Wall Outlives the Siege
Every assault the formation survives becomes structural memory that reinforces its next defence without erasing the cost already paid.

Serious wounds become “graven,” heavily reinforcing that region against repeat damage; wounded limbs and joints are structurally braced to function longer, repeat strikes against a graven region suffer violent contact recoil, and accumulating wounds improve her stance, stability and resistance to displacement. Counterplay is varied targeting, internal / circulation disruption, exhaustion, overwhelming damage or incapacitation.
Connects graven-region reinforcement into her shield and spear structure, turning survived wounds into hardened defensive framework.
Delays catastrophic functional consequences while Sigrun stays conscious and sustains the Dominion — it does not heal her, and the accumulated consequences catch up the moment the Dominion ends.
arcFigures.firstArc: Continuation Chronicle — When Wuyue Marches North
arcFigures.affiliationRole: The First Wall — field commander of the 72,000-strong First Banner Army

arcFigures.name: Halvek Veyrhald
arcFigures.subtitle: The Gate Road · Peak Sovereign · Veyrhald military architect
arcFigures.details: A road-and-gate specialist who makes lawful military access answer to his position. He is strongest while holding a connected defence and progressively more burdened when forced to maintain many isolated junctions himself. Final arc: killed holding a vital gate / road network during the Shinsei opening invasion, Jun’s breach pressure central to the defeat.
skills: Every Road Kneels Before the Gate
Connected military roads become extensions of one defended gate, allowing Halvek to close, redirect or reinforce them through a single governing formation.
arcFigures.firstEpisodeTitle: Liang Finds Two Circulations in One War
arcFigures.firstArc: Continuation Chronicle — When Wuyue Marches North
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Keeper of the Gate Roads — military-road and fortress-seal architect

arcFigures.name: Solveig Skeldran
arcFigures.subtitle: The Last Snow · High Sovereign · Skeldran hunt commander
arcFigures.details: Skeldran’s greatest pursuit authority. Once she receives a genuine trace, she can continue reconstructing its path across distance and concealment until the trail ends or is deliberately divided among valid successors. Final arc: survives wounded and becomes Isgard’s Acting War Commander while the Paragons are incapacitated.
skills: No Footprint Survives the Last Snow
One genuine footprint becomes a continuous pursuit route through every later concealment, false trail and transferred command.
arcFigures.firstArc: Continuation Chronicle — When Wuyue Marches North
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Acting War Commander (final arc) · senior Huntmistress

arcFigures.name: Raska Dravaryn
arcFigures.subtitle: The Setting-Sun Cavalry · High Sovereign · Dravaryn field commander
arcFigures.details: A mounted Dravaryn commander who preserves the completed momentum of one cavalry assault inside the next. She remains a disciplined continental defender rather than a disposable extension of Maedra’s ambition. Final arc: killed in a countercharge against Kenji’s Stormstep Dominion during the opening invasion.
skills: Crimson Cavalry Crosses the Setting Sun
The momentum of each completed cavalry charge is retained and layered into the next until terrain, formation or deliberate restraint breaks the sequence.
arcFigures.firstArc: Continuation Chronicle — Where the Black Wick Leads

arcFigures.name: Eldran Dravaryn
arcFigures.subtitle: The Cinder Standard · High Sovereign · Dravaryn ground commander
arcFigures.details: A patient territorial commander whose planted standard stores heat, force and formation authority in every mile his army has successfully held, then releases that prepared ground beneath an enemy’s technique. Final arc: survives but is permanently retired / crippled after shielding Maedra from a killing sequence.
skills: Cinder Standard Over the Fallen Mile
Every secured stretch of ground stores the formation’s marching force and heat, allowing Eldran to make an enemy contest the land beneath a battle rather than its visible surface.
arcFigures.firstEpisodeTitle: The Imperial Army Holds Its First Foreign Line
arcFigures.firstArc: Continuation Chronicle — When Wuyue Marches North

arcFigures.name: Maedra Dravaryn
arcFigures.subtitle: The Crimson Road · Stable Paragon · Senior Dravaryn war authority
arcFigures.details: The senior Dravaryn war authority, ranked above Raska Dravaryn, and the coalition's war architect commanding its primary offensive. A newly established but stable Paragon, she pursues a war meant to make Dravaryn the military center of Isgard and reduce Veyrhald's legal primacy to ceremony. Final arc: survives but is critically injured in the opening invasion.
skills: Supreme Domain Skill · Domain / Internal Assault
Every wound Maedra earns or formally claims becomes an internal road through which later techniques can bypass exterior protection.
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Coalition war architect — senior war authority above Raska

arcFigures.name: Ren Qiao
arcFigures.subtitle: Yuecheng physician and innkeeper
arcFigures.details: A Yuecheng physician whose hands are permanently stained with herbal ink. She runs the inn where Sera and Rhen first stay in the moonless city and explains that its people have gone years without a moon or restful sleep.
arcFigures.firstArc: The City Without a Moon

arcFigures.name: Jae Miri
arcFigures.subtitle: Unranked mid-Marquis weapon specialist
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Weapon specialist / Arin’s Season 23 test opponent
arcFigures.details: An unranked mid-Marquis specialist whose segmented staff changes between short staff, spear and linked blades through internal tension. She tests Arin Vale in the temple courtyard and forces Arin to adapt to changing weapon geometry before surrendering cleanly.
arcFigures.firstArc: Rank Transition

arcFigures.name: Mareth Duskvein
arcFigures.subtitle: Keeper of the Last Pulse · Head of Duskvein
arcFigures.affiliationRole: Guild head / Keeper of the Last Pulse
arcFigures.details: Duskvein’s austere leader and the primary antagonist of the Bannerfall crisis. His basin lattice reaches Peak Sovereign pressure approaching Paragon by borrowing force from prepared poison anchors and dependent bodies; it resembles a Dominion from outside but is not one.
arcFigures.firstArc: Where the Black Wick Leads

arcFigures.name: Garran Duskvein
arcFigures.subtitle: The Iron Leech · Duskvein First Executioner
arcFigures.details: Duskvein’s High Sovereign execution chief. Garran uses iron-ring circulation systems linked to the prison lattice and is responsible for breaking prestigious captives for public display, concentrating his cruelty on Ilyra when her dual meridians resist the poison network.
arcFigures.firstArc: Where the Black Wick Leads

arcFigures.name: Eira Eirholt
arcFigures.subtitle: Winter Physician · defensive Sovereign and mass stabilizer
arcFigures.details: A senior Eirholt physician assessed by Quiet Hands at Established Sovereign. Her cultivation is built around defense, survival and mass stabilization rather than dueling. She turns Eirholt against Duskvein’s Rank Four claim after proving its treatment records and medical neutrality were falsified.
arcFigures.firstArc: Where the Black Wick Leads

arcFigures.name: Tor Veyrhald
arcFigures.subtitle: Iron Witness · High Sovereign · Veyrhald envoy and Ledger authority
arcFigures.details: An older High Sovereign spear practitioner sent by first-ranked Veyrhald. Tor is explicitly not among Veyrhald’s strongest three; he carries Gate Seal and Ledger authority, protects lawful surrender and insists that evidence survive scrutiny before continental force is committed. Final arc: survives but permanently retires from frontline combat after overforcing damaged circulation under Nao’s control.
arcFigures.firstEpisodeTitle: The First Banner Does Not Applaud
arcFigures.firstArc: Where the Black Wick Leads

arcFigures.name: Brynja Kharvorn
arcFigures.subtitle: Established Sovereign · Kharvorn coastal-defence commander · Iron Fjord
arcFigures.details: Commander of Kharvorn’s Iron Fjord forces, specializing in amphibious heavy infantry, landing denial and iron-hulled shore engines. During the Rimewall encirclement she controls the shore engines and anchors used to trap Shen Rui’s retreat routes.
arcFigures.firstArc: When Wuyue Marches North

arcFigures.name: Oskar Solvane
arcFigures.subtitle: Solvane Sovereign commander · Winterglass Lances
arcFigures.details: Commander of Solvane’s Winterglass Lances, a nine-thousand-strong long-spear cavalry force built to punish retreat. At Rimewall he seals Shen Rui’s northern withdrawal routes and repeatedly attacks the exact supply roads Rui had maintained for the hospital fleet.
arcFigures.firstArc: When Wuyue Marches North

arcFigures.name: Astrid Vardrenn
arcFigures.subtitle: Mid Sovereign · Vardrenn recon / hidden-road commander · Black Pine Wardens
arcFigures.details: Commander of Vardrenn’s Black Pine Wardens, an eight-thousand-strong force specializing in forest scouts, longbows, hidden roads and defensive ambush corridors. She holds fire when Sera exposes both armies and moves civilians through the contested corridor in plain sight.
arcFigures.firstEpisodeTitle: Veiled Moon Cannot Hide an Army
arcFigures.firstArc: When Wuyue Marches North

arcFigures.name: Jorek Norrvek
arcFigures.subtitle: Norrvek Sovereign commander · Chainforge Assembly
arcFigures.details: Commander of Norrvek’s eight-thousand-strong Chainforge Assembly. His institution links siege chains, mobile walls, bridge capture and anti-fortification engineering into one command rhythm, making Norrvek structurally vital even when stronger Sovereigns exist elsewhere in the coalition.
arcFigures.firstEpisodeTitle: Twenty Percent Does Not March Like an Army
arcFigures.firstArc: When Wuyue Marches North

arcFigures.name: Freya Ysmark
arcFigures.subtitle: Ysmark Sovereign commander · Pale Wolf Banner
arcFigures.details: Commander of Ysmark’s seven-thousand-strong Pale Wolf Banner, specializing in pack pursuit, broken-ground skirmishing and recovery of isolated units. She suspends Pale Wolf recovery operations and demands an internal hearing after released prisoners prove that Duskvein falsified the deaths and routes of Ysmark companies.
arcFigures.firstArc: When Wuyue Marches North

arcFigures.name: Kellan Haldren
arcFigures.subtitle: Haldren Sovereign commander · Ash-Horn Spears
arcFigures.details: Commander of Haldren’s six-thousand Ash-Horn Spears, known for dense spear blocks, reserve reinforcement and disciplined attritional defense. Bound by an old oath to Veyrhald’s lawful continental defense, Kellan refuses Maedra’s unsigned Hearth order and withdraws rather than turn civilians into a military roadblock.
arcFigures.firstArc: When Wuyue Marches North

23.description: Receives a full final arc before the fatal setup.

24.name: Qin Luo

25.description: Uses already-revealed Spring After Snow; no new Supreme Art.

28.description: Returns vastly stronger after assimilating parts of Jiang's cultivation architecture.

28.description: His final duel and stolen cultivation architecture drive the new arc.

29.name: Yun Shizhen
29.description: Uses Ten Thousand Venoms Become One.

29.description: Defeats the Marquises after they force him to reveal all nine evolved Wheels.

30.description: Begins the long rematch with Huo.

32.name: Huo Wujin
32.description: Survives Rhen's defeat and remains a terrifying restrained wild card.

33.description: Refines healing, abandons sword reliance and begins forming Petals in Stasis.

33.name: Valeria Nox
33.description: Saint of the Last Step; nearly defeats Lei.

34.description: Mirror Queen; coldly cruel, methodical and clearly above Jin in direct combat.

35.description: First Catastrophe; strongest subordinate Crown and already above the known summit.

35.name: Sera
35.description: Faces Draven again with Marquis support while still injured.

35.name: Rhen
35.description: Still absent and unaware during the third season of the five-season seclusion arc.

36.name: Kael Veyran

36.description: Survives another brutal Valeria encounter but cannot defeat Crown IV.

36.description: Recognizes the Crowns are measuring the entire eastern hierarchy but still withholds the emergency message.

36.name: Sera
36.description: Is gravely injured again by Draven.

36.description: Still unaware during the fourth season of his absence.

39.description: Tests Kael and prepares as second-line summit response.

73.description: Peak Marquis-class acting commander beneath Ilyra and the Crownless Host’s temporary leader when Ilyra departs.

75.name: Qin Luo and Lu Weiran

76.name: Tae Muyeon and Huo Wujin

78.name: Varok Skeldran

canonRules.title: Recurring Character Reintroduction Rule
canonRules.text: Because the cast is large, every recurring named character must be naturally reintroduced when returning after a meaningful absence, at the start of a new season/arc, or when their identity may no longer be obvious. The reintroduction should briefly remind the reader of their role, rank/title or affiliation, and the one relationship or prior event that matters to the current scene. Do not dump a full biography and do not write meta phrases such as 'as readers remember'. Major core leads Sera and Rhen need only light contextual reminders.

canonRules.title: Long-Gap Character Memory Rule
canonRules.text: If a named character has been absent for roughly two seasons or more, reintroduce them naturally at their next meaningful mention—even if they only appear as a historical comparison. Include title/rank or affiliation plus the past event that matters to the current scene. Historical names such as Huo Wujin are not exempt.

canonRules.title: Six Crowns Power Rule
canonRules.text: Every elite Crown individually outranks any single Duke. Crown V leaves #7–#10 critical and cannot be defeated by Sera; she only delays him long enough to save them. Crown IV repeatedly defeats Lei despite his adaptations. Crown II forces Jin to escape and requires multi-Duke responses. Crown I decisively defeats Tae and Kael separately. Vaelor crushes all Five Dukes together, tortures #4 Lei close to death, then outmaneuvers Kael and Tae together and leaves both near death. Pre-seclusion Rhen could still defeat Vaelor; post-seclusion Rhen is incomparably beyond him.

canonRules.title: Rhen Post-Seclusion Rule
canonRules.text: Rhen remains fully unaware in seclusion throughout Seasons 33–37. Jin prepares an emergency route earlier but does not send the message until Season 37 Episode 9; Rhen receives it only at the final beat of Episode 10. He returns in Season 38, no longer needs a sword for serious combat, and ordinary physical injury self-corrects almost instantly. Heaven's Return can independently heal up to ten people inside an indestructible hemisphere. Winter Has No Horizon is demonstrated as a principle in Season 39 and first used in combat in Season 42. Petals in Stasis is named and theorized privately in Season 42 but first activated in Season 58; Petals Beneath a Frozen Moon is finally revealed once in Season 59 against Aethon.

canonRules.title: Arc VIII Structure
canonRules.text: Seasons 33–37 are Arc VIII Part I — The Six Crowns: Western Dark. Seasons 38–42 are Part II — Crown Beyond Crowns. Season 43 is the aftermath coda: recovery, romance, Crown Accord beginnings, and Vaelor's warning about far older western powers.

canonRules.title: Season 43 Aftermath Rule
canonRules.text: Season 43 lowers the combat intensity, restores romance and recovery, and ends with Vaelor warning that the Six Crowns were only the visible shield of the west. Ancient powers older than the current ranking world are beginning to wake.

canonRules.title: Final Saga Power Hierarchy
canonRules.text: During the final major saga, every Ancient King drastically supersedes Vaelor in baseline physical strength, speed, durability, internal strength and qi reserves before signature arts are considered. King VII is weakest; King I Amon is strongest. Aethon is substantially above Amon. Rhen remains vastly beyond Aethon.

canonRules.title: Ilyra #6 Rule
canonRules.text: After Sera retires, Ilyra Serath becomes World #6. During the Ancient King war she is stronger than several Dukes in direct combat, while Kael, Tae and Liang remain above her overall. She repeatedly protects Marquises and injured Dukes and declines upward ranking challenges. Sera's later growth beyond Duke level does not change the board because Sera remains retired.

canonRules.title: Sera Retirement and Passive Timeline
canonRules.text: Sera and Rhen retire immediately after Vaelor's defeat. One year later Rhen develops A Thousand Petals Without Falling. Sera spends the following full year inside its one-mile passive refinement field. The Ancient Kings invade two years after Vaelor's defeat, and Sera returns at legitimate Duke level while remaining retired. In the two-year Second Spring epilogue, continued passive refinement carries her beyond the old Duke framework.

canonRules.title: Final Major Arc Structure
canonRules.text: Seasons 44–53 form Final Major Arc Part I — The Seven Thrones. Seasons 54–63 form Final Major Arc Part II — The Sovereign Before Heaven. Season 64 is a three-episode epilogue set two peaceful years later at Second Spring, showing Sera beyond Duke level and Rhen beyond useful measurement.

canonRules.title: Orun Earth Burial Rule
canonRules.text: Ancient King VII Orun Vhal, the Buried Sovereign, cultivates Earth Burial. Natural earth, stone, dust and sand act as extensions of his martial body. Buried Heaven stores and releases force through terrain; Sandsea Funeral weaponizes qi-infused sand; Earthbound King diverts damage into natural ground; The World Beneath Your Feet Is Mine is his Transcended domain. Removing Orun from continuous natural terrain is the central counter and explains Rui's artificial-water battlefields.
